payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Change the image into pencil drawing
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the image visibly appear as a completed pencil drawing?
node.criteria: Compose both supports under R1 without treating either support as completion credit by itself. Complete (yes) only when s1 passes. Partial only when s1 does not pass, s2 passes, and the evidence is sufficient to establish some requested progress without complete fulfillment. Absent (no) only when s1 fails and s2 fails, with sufficient evidence that no requested change has progressed. Unknown when required evidence is unresolved, including when s1 is unknown and completion cannot be established, or when s2 is unknown and absence or partial progress cannot be established. Unrelated edits never count as progress.
node.binding: Target: The image is rendered as a pencil drawing, with its visual content represented in a pencil-drawn style.. Reference: The supplied image and the requested pencil-drawing transformation..

node_traces.evidence: Both saved supports pass: s1 establishes that the edited image preserves the meal and table setting in a pencil-drawn style, and s2 independently reports visible sketch-like shading and outlines. Under the saved criteria, s1 passing is sufficient for completion.

dependencies.evidence: The edited image preserves the original meal and table setting while rendering them in a muted, grainy, pencil-drawn style.

The edited image shows a visible pencil-drawing-style treatment: colors are muted and the food and surrounding objects have sketch-like shading and outlines, indicating progress toward the requested style.

response.content: {"text":"The node’s binding asks whether the image appears as a *completed* pencil drawing, but its criteria make s1 passing sufficient for “yes.” That lets evidence of a muted, grainy pencil-like treatment override the distinction between visible progress and completion; s2’s wording (“indicating progress”) also does not establish completion. Tighten the typed decision logic so completion requires evidence that the requested transformation is substantially realized across the image, while partial requires supported visible progress that falls short, and absent requires supported lack of progress. Apply those thresholds to the actual source/edit comparison: the edit visibly changes the meal and setting into a pale, grainy, sketch-like rendering, but the traces do not explain why that amounts to a completed drawing rather than partial progress. Require the supports to distinguish those states explicitly and ground their judgments in visual evidence, rather than treating two correlated “pass” labels as independent proof. Preserve unknown when evidence cannot resolve the distinction. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated here; the mismatch is semantic calibration and criterion ambiguity."}
